name: bathroom-rate-card-partial
note: The real recording that priced itself two ways on 2026-08-10 and 2026-08-11: $450 one run, $513.36 the next, from a byte-identical transcript. Both obeyed the no-splitting rule — the difference was the toilet line. Named 'New toilet' and typed material it matched nothing; named 'Remove old toilet and fit new one' and typed labor it matched the saved 'Toilet Installation' rate and took $63.36. That match is also wrong on its own terms: the rate prices FITTING a toilet, and the job also supplies one, so the priced version quietly under-quoted by the cost of a toilet. Expected behaviour: the toilet line stays unpriced either way. 'New sink with vanity unit' is named identically in the rate card and should match every time.
transcript: Right, this one's for Marina Kapanadze, apartment 12 on Chavchavadze Avenue. Bathroom renovation. She wants the old toilet taken out and a new one fitted, plus a new sink with the vanity unit. Two mixer taps — no wait, three, one for the kitchen as well. About eight meters of pipe, the 20 mil stuff. There's also a leaking valve behind the wall I need to replace, I don't know what that costs yet, I have to check with the supplier. Day and a half of work, call it 400 for the labor. Tell her it's good for two weeks and she needs to pay half upfront.
